purpose: A container used to hold titles, subtitles, buttons, and input elements. Appears at the top or bottom of a screen, dialog, or popover to provide navigation, actions, and key content. Defines start (left) and end (right) content areas.
whenToUse: Display page headers, subheaders, footers, and floating footers on a page, dialog, or popover
Include only a small number of components (up to two interactive elements)
As a header bar: with or without a Back/Home navigation button
As a footer bar: fixed at the bottom providing final actions
As a floating footer bar: stays visible above content when scrolling
whenNotToUse: Don't use for many components that require overflow — use Toolbar instead
Don't use when responsive overflow handling is needed — use OverflowToolbar
doRules: Limit the number of actions within the bar
Use full width of the screen for the bar
Place the bar at the top of a container to provide contextual actions and information
Place the footer bar at the bottom of the page or container to provide final actions
Use bar with subheader variant on mobile when space is limited
Center content is supported but not recommended — align to start instead
dontRules: Don't use bar when more than two interactive elements are needed — use toolbar
Don't rely on bar for overflow behavior — it is not supported

layoutGuidance.placement: Top (header/subheader) or bottom (footer/floating footer) of page, dialog, or popover.
layoutGuidance.sizing: Full width of parent container. Height auto.
layoutGuidance.alignment: Start content: left-aligned (navigation, back buttons, titles). End content: right-aligned (action buttons, icons). Centered content: supported but not recommended.

contentGuidance.labelLength: Keep titles concise. Action button labels: verb-first imperative (Confirm, Cancel).
contentRules: Start area: navigation elements — back buttons, titles, menus, logos
End area: action buttons, icons, user profiles
Busy state supported: use BusyIndicator (sizes: small, medium, large; default: medium)
Bar itself has no states except busy — elements inside have their own states
Supports LTR and RTL — action buttons end-aligned in both directions
examples: Floating footer: stays visible above content when scrolling

responsiveBehavior.XL: Full header bar with all elements
responsiveBehavior.L: Full header bar with all elements
responsiveBehavior.M: Use bar with subheader to distribute content when space is limited
responsiveBehavior.S: Bar with subheader on mobile; header bar on desktop

accessibilityGuidance.requirement: Tab: navigates through items. Shift+Tab: backward. F6: moves focus to next UI group. Shift+F6: backward.

incompatible: More than 2 interactive elements — use Toolbar instead

exceptions: Floating footer bar moves with scroll and is always visible at bottom — differs from fixed footer
Bar itself is only a container — no component states except busy state
types: Header bar: container header, with or without navigation button
Bar with subheader: additional subheader below main header (subtitle, search, etc.)
Footer bar: fixed at bottom of container
Floating footer bar: scrolls with content, always visible at screen bottom
